_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). MIXED, and split hard by height: the TOP THIRD (y 0-0.30) is a continuous grove canopy -- three overlapping crowns of double-outline oval leaves (夾葉) in blue-green wash, hung on two heavy ochre trunks, with a curtain of drooping creeper strands on the left; the BOTTOM TWO THIRDS (y 0.30-1.0) is the foreground bank, all rock and exposed root, textured with long parallel 牛毛皴 hair strokes and NO green. The one trap in this tile is a set of pink/ochre stroke-fans at y 0.28-0.42 that read as autumn grass at a glance -- zoomed in they terminate on the boulder contour lines and are texture strokes on rounded rock. They are labelled rock. Real foliage outside the canopy: a bamboo/reed clump at the lower left, an orchid tuft clipped by the left edge, and faded sprigs on the far bank across the water. No seals, no figures except one robe hem clipped by the top edge.

objects.name: left crown of double-outline oval leaves
objects.note: dense 夾葉 -- each leaf a closed dark outline filled with blue-green wash, clustered in 介-shaped sprays. Clipped by the top edge; the rest of this crown is in t002 directly above. Good hinge subject, well separated from rock

objects.name: curtain of creeper strands hanging leaf sprays
objects.note: SPARSE BY NATURE -- thin threads dropping from the canopy, each carrying a small five-lobed leaf cluster, with bare silk and pale rock between them. A later reader will look at this box and think it is loose; it is not, the subject itself is a curtain. Do not tighten it into the strands, and do not fill it -- alpha the mask from the leaf glyphs, not the box

objects.name: faded low sprigs on the far bank across the water
objects.note: badly worn, pale blue-green, small. Easy to miss and easy to dismiss as silk stain -- they are leaves, on the far side of the stream. Far depth: they belong to a different parallax plane from the near canopy

objects.name: central crown between the two trunks
objects.note: the densest leaf mass in the tile. NOTE THE HOLE: a pink-washed rock face shows through a gap at roughly [0.56,0.14,0.63,0.20] -- the box is honest but not solid, so the mask must come from the leaf outlines, not from filling the rectangle

objects.name: right crown, running off the right edge
objects.note: same 夾葉 species as the left crown. Leaf tongues hang across the main trunk at x 0.75-0.80 -- those leaves move, the bark under them does not. Continues into t007 (which overlaps this tile by 77%)

objects.name: solid black-ink lanceolate leaf cluster
objects.note: A DIFFERENT SPECIES sitting inside the right crown: filled black strokes, no outline, no wash, needle/lance shaped. Reads as a dark blotch at tile scale and could be mistaken for a shadow or an ink stain. It is foliage and it should move on its own beat, not with the blue-green leaves around it

objects.name: bamboo and reed clump on the lower-left bank
objects.note: long blue-green blades fanning from a rock crevice, drawn one stroke per blade. The nearest vegetation in the tile and the only foliage in the bottom half -- if the grove above is animated and this stays frozen the foreground reads as dead. Right-hand blades at x 0.30-0.40 are faded to grey; still leaves

objects.name: orchid-grass tuft clipped by the left edge
objects.note: only the right tips are in frame; the whole tuft is in t005 at its x 1050-1300. Verified against t005 before labelling

objects.name: pale water at the left edge
objects.note: featureless pale silk HERE, which is why it is easy to call empty -- but t005 shows the ripple lines and the far bank a few hundred px to the left, so this is the tail of the stream, not blank silk. Any ripple treatment must be continuous with t005, not started fresh at the tile seam

objects.name: left trunk with a heavy vine coiled around it
objects.note: ochre bark with a thick knobbly liana looped around it three times. The liana is woody, not a leafy vine -- it is structure and it must NOT move. Runs down into the root mass below

objects.name: the great knotted trunk, centre-right
objects.note: the widest trunk in the tile, with burl knots and hollow eyes. Leaves from both neighbouring crowns overlap its edges -- keep the bark out of the foliage mask or the whole tree will sway like a card

objects.name: the mass of exposed looping roots across the bank
objects.note: great tan ropes coiling over the rock, drawn with double contour lines and a light wash. Structurally trunk, not rock, and rigid either way. The most visually restless passage in the lower half -- an automatic motion detector will want to move it. It must not

objects.name: band of rounded boulders under the canopy
objects.note: THE TRAP IN THIS TILE. Carries fans of fine tapered parallel strokes under a warm pink/ochre wash -- at tile scale this reads as autumn grass or a hanging fringe of leaves. Zoomed in, every stroke follows the dome of the stone and stops dead on the boulder's contour line, and there is no green anywhere in it. This is 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre texture. A colour-threshold mask that keys on warm tones will grab this and animate the rock -- the exact defect that got the earlier pass rejected

objects.name: dark ink rock shelf on the left
objects.note: heavy wet ink, the darkest rock in the tile. Sits behind the vine curtain -- creeper strands cross it, so a mask cut by darkness alone will lose the leaves in front

objects.name: the broad foreground bank filling the bottom
objects.note: long sweeping contour strokes with dry-brush texture, darkening to wet ink boulders at the very bottom edge (y > 0.85). This is the bottom of the scroll. Nothing here moves except the bamboo clump boxed separately

objects.name: hem of a standing figure's robe, top-left corner
objects.note: only the lower robe and its fold lines are in frame; head, sleeve and sash are in t002 directly above (verified there). Left in 留白 -- undyed silk with contour lines only. If this tile is treated in isolation the shape reads as a pale rock; it is a person
